column1: # gate-guards.tsv -- every construct in a gate script that lets it decline to fail.
# A gate is only as good as its narrowest escape hatch. `|| true`, a discarded
# stderr, and a warning where an error belongs are all ways for a check to
# report success without having checked. Some are correct -- grep exits 1 on no
# match, and an advisory step is allowed to be advisory -- but each one has to
# be a decision somebody made on purpose rather than a habit.
# So: every matching line in validate-grammar.sh, parse-al-parallel.sh and
# tools/tree-harness.sh must appear here with a reason. Add a guard without a
# row and the sweep fails; delete a guard and leave its row and the sweep fails
# too, so this file cannot drift into a rubber stamp.
# Three tab-separated fields: file, the guard line (whitespace-collapsed), and
# why it is allowed to degrade. Regenerate the keys with:

column3: diff exits 1 whenever it finds a difference, which is the expected case here. The verdict comes from the awk rewriter, which aborts on any unrecognised line and requires emitted == changed.
Deliberately best-effort: one warm parse to close a cold-cache window before fanning out. Its failure changes nothing, because every chunk is parsed and counted afterwards.

column2: print_warning "query-coverage: corpus not present (BC.History missing) — skipping, see tools/query_coverage/README.md"
column3: Gated on BC.History actually being absent, so exit 2 for any other reason (drifted corpus, stale baseline) still fails. Deliberate, and documented at the step.

Not a degradation: this is the FAILING branch. A non-zero census exit is split into 'cases were dropped' (a real defect -- print_error, VALIDATION_FAILED=1) and 'the counter itself broke' (also an error, different message). The `||` is a second detection route, not an escape hatch: DROPPED_CASES may be empty when the counter died before printing it, and the grep still finds the rows.

column2: print_warning "Corpus file census SKIPPED — not a git work tree (expected under gate_selftest); $CORPUS_ON_DISK file(s) on disk"
column3: The disk-vs-index comparison needs a git work tree, and gate_selftest.py runs gates in a bare scratch copy WITHOUT .git on purpose. Unguarded, this check would fail every self-test case for an unrelated reason. It warns and never reports success -- an unrunnable check must not read as a census that found nothing.

grep exits 1 on no match, which would abort under `set -e` when the corpus is empty. The `|| true` yields 0, and 0 tracked against N on disk is exactly the mismatch the next line fails on -- the guard cannot mask the defect it guards.

column2: print_warning "Corpus file census SKIPPED — 0 tracked beside $CORPUS_ON_DISK on disk, so this is a copy outside the index (expected under gate_selftest)"
column3: A scratch COPY of the repo can sit INSIDE the real work tree, which is where gate_selftest puts one on a CI runner: git rev-parse says yes while git ls-files resolves against the copy and returns nothing. Gated on 0 tracked beside a NON-EMPTY disk, a state no real clone has ever been in, so a genuinely untracked fixture in a real checkout (1 of N) still fails.
